1 INTRODUCTION

This document outlines the statistical methods to be implemented in the analysis of data collected within the scope of Spectrum Pharmaceuticals, Inc. Protocol SPI-611 “A Multicenter, Randomized Phase 3 Trial of Single-Dose Intravesical EOquin as a Surgical Adjuvant Instilled in the Early Postoperative Period in Patients Undergoing Transurethral Resection for Noninvasive Bladder Cancer”. The purpose of this plan is to provide methods of analysis and the presentation of results of all data collected. This plan provides detailed analysis of all efficacy and safety variables including primary endpoint and all other efficacy endpoints. The statistical plan described here includes a priori plan that was submitted prior to unblinding the study and additional analyses of subgroups to support efficacy endpoints. This plan will supersede definitions and procedures described in any other past or present documents regarding the statistical analyses of the efficacy and safety endpoints of Study
2 OBJECTIVES
The primary objective of the study is:
To evaluate the recurrence rate of bladder cancer at 2 years in patients with TURBT
plus EOquin versus those who receive TURBT plus placebo. The secondary objectives of the study are:
1. To evaluate time to first recurrence in patients who receive TURBT plus EOquin
versus those who receive TURBT plus placebo.
2. To evaluate progression to higher stage or grade, number of recurrences per patient,
and overall survival.
3. To assess the safety of EOquin instilled into the bladder in the early postoperative
period.
4. To assess functional bladder capacity in a 150 patient subset of randomized
patients.
3 STUDY OVERVIEW

This is a multi-center, randomized trial. After screening procedures are performed, appropriate patients will undergo a TURBT. Following TUR of all visible tumors, patients meeting all of the inclusion/exclusion criteria will be randomized to receive either EOquin or Placebo, reconstituted with 20 mL of diluent and 20 mL of sterile water (total volume 40
mL) instilled into the bladder within 6 hours of the end of the TUR procedure. EOquin or

Placebo will be retained for 60 minutes, following which it will be drained from the bladder. If there are no complications, the patient will be discharged. The patient will be seen for a postoperative follow-up exam 21±10 days after the TUR. At this time, the pathology report will be reviewed. If the histology of the patient’s tumor is confirmed Ta, G1-G2 (low grade, WHO/ISUP classification), then the patient will receive no further treatment and will be observed cystoscopically every three months through year two for tumor recurrence. If the histology of the patient’s tumor is other than Ta, G1 or G2 (low

grade, WHO/ISUP classification), then the patient will be free to receive further treatment in accordance with current treatment guidelines, and will be followed up cystoscopically every three months through year two for tumor recurrence. All patients will be followed for two years.
3.1 Visit Definitions
Data will be summarized by visit. A patient may or may not have come to the clinic at the scheduled visit time per protocol. Therefore, non-overlapping intervals are defined for visits.

blocks.text: The visit windows should not contain multiple observations for a patient that fall into the same time window. However, if the visit windows do contain multiple observations the following rules will be used. For most analyses, the observation that is closest to the target day will be used. For laboratory data, the “worst case” observation will be used, where “worst case” is defined as the highest toxicity grade or the most abnormal value.
3.2 Experimental Design

This trial is a double-blind randomized, two-arm, recurrence rate, clinical trial of patients with noninvasive bladder cancer rendered free of tumor by TURBT. The trial is designed to compare TURBT plus EOquin versus TURBT plus placebo in the treatment of noninvasive bladder cancer. Patients are randomized after TURBT and followed for 24 months. 4 DEFINITIONS AND ALGORITHMS
4.1 Derived Variables

Baseline: Day of Transurethral Resection of Bladder Tumor performed at Week 0. Study duration: Date of the last patient visit minus date of randomization. Recurrence: Appearance of new, histologically confirmed, bladder tumor while on study. Recurrence rate: The proportion of patients with histologically confirmed recurrence of the bladder tumor at any time after randomization and on or before Year 2. The first recurrence will be used for recurrence rate. Date of recurrence: The date of the first cystoscopically confirmed recurrence. The confirmation of the recurrence will be made using the central independent pathology report. The detailed algorithm of determination of recurrence and time to recurrence is provided in Section 5.5.2. Time to recurrence: Time from randomization to date of first histologically confirmed recurrence of the patients’ bladder tumor. Patients without recurrence by Month 24 cystoscopy assessment visit will be considered to be censored at the last available visit/contact. Patients who died due to any cause before confirmed recurrence by Month 24

cystoscopy assessment visit will be considered progressed with date of death as the date. If the date of death is after Month 24 cystoscopy assessment visit without a recurrence, the patient will be censored at 24 months. If a patient had a suspected lesion and died before histological confirmation, the date of suspected recurrence will be used as the date of
recurrence. The detailed algorithm for the determination of recurrence and time to recurrence

is provided in Section 5.5.2. Data on recurrence of bladder tumor is collected for patients who drop out of the study prior to recurrence of disease. However, the frequency of assessments on these patients may not match those for patients remaining in the study. To evaluate the effect of using follow-up data for recurrence on these patients, additional analyses will be conducted excluding data from this group. Patients who withdraw from the study before recurrence will be censored at the date of withdrawal from the study for this additional analysis. Overall survival: The number of months from randomization to death from any cause. Disease-free survival (DFS): The number of months from randomization to histologically confirmed recurrence of the patient’s bladder tumor or death from any cause. Disease-free interval (DFI): The number of months from randomization to histologically confirmed progression to higher stage or grade of the patient’s bladder tumor or death from any cause. This definition was requested by FDA as part of the SPA agreement. Time to progression: Time from randomization to date of first histologically confirmed progression to higher stage or grade of the patients’ bladder tumor. Patients without recurrence will be considered to be censored at the last available visit/contact. Patients who died due to any cause before confirmed recurrence will be considered to be censored on the date of death.
4.2 Data Handling Conventions
4.2.1 Data Adjustments/Handling/Conventions

All data collected on the Cases Report Forms (CRFs) will be presented in listings. Data not subject to analysis according to this plan will not appear in any tables or graphs but will be included in the data listings. All p-values will be displayed in four decimals and always rounded up (e.g., 0.XXXX). If a p-value less than 0.0001 occurs it will be shown in tables as <0.0001. All percentages will be displayed round to the nearest tenth. Treatment emergent adverse events will be defined as events not seen at baseline or events that worsened in severity even if present at baseline. Baseline adverse events will also be presented separately. Laboratory values comes from central laboratory using standard units. Central laboratory data will be flagged as L or H for values below or above the normal range. Months will be calculated as number of days/30.437.
4.2.2 Missing information

Except as noted here, missing data will not be imputed. That is, the analyses will be performed using the observed data only. Some prior or follow-up dates may be missing partially. Missing years will not be estimated. Year only dates will be imputed for prior dates only (e.g. date of first diagnosis), where st missing month and day will be estimated to be July 1 . Missing day of a known month will th be estimated to be 15 Derived variables like duration and time to recurrence will be based on estimated dates.
5 STATISTICAL METHODS
5.1 General Analysis Considerations
The statistical analyses will be reported using summary tables, figures, and data listings. All analyses and tabulations will be performed using SAS® Version 9.1 or higher on a PC
platform. If the use of other software is warranted, the final statistical methodology report

will detail what software is used and for what purpose. All tables, listings, and figures will be validated and reviewed before being finalized. Independent programming will be conducted to verify tables and listings as appropriate. Tables will be reviewed for accuracy, consistency with this plan, consistency within tables, and consistency with corresponding output. For the continuous variables, number of non-missing values and mean, standard deviation, median, minimum and maximum will be tabulated by treatment group. For the categorical variables, the counts and percent for each possible value will be tabulated by treatment
group. Treatment groups will be compared using chi-square (with continuity correction) or
Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test and two-sided 95% confidence intervals will be provided for proportions and difference in proportions. For time to event data, the log rank test will be
used. The distribution of time will be displayed using Kaplan-Meier curves. Hazard ratio and
its 95% confidence interval will be provided.
5.2 Sample Size

The sample size was determined using the software nQuery Advisor 6.01 (Statistical Solutions Ltd., Cork, Ireland). This study has 1:1 randomization (TURBT plus EOquin vs. TURBT plus placebo). All patients will be assigned to one of the two treatment arms. Based on a 2-sided test at the 5% significance level, a total of 562 patients randomized to TURBT plus EOquin or TURBT plus placebo (281 per treatment group) will provide 80% power to detect a 12% reduction in the recurrence rate at year 2 for patients treated with TURBT plus EOquin from an assumed 48% recurrence rate at year 2 for patients treated with TURBT plus placebo. The randomizing physician must visually estimate the stage and grade of the bladder tumors removed prior to randomization and ensure they appear to be Ta, G1 or Ta, G2. Since randomized study treatment must be administered within 6 hours of TURBT, patients must be randomized prior to definite staging and grading of the tumor by the pathologist. We estimate the randomizing physician will be incorrect in their visual assessment of tumor stage and grade approximately 28% of the time. Therefore, up to 800 patients will be enrolled in
order to achieve the target enrollment of 562 Ta, G1 or Ta, G2 patients randomized to TURBT plus EOquin or TURBT plus placebo.
5.3 Randomization

Patients will be randomized 1:1 to either EOquin or placebo. The randomization plan will use a permuted block design and will not be stratified by prognostic factors. However, patients will be randomized within center with a block size of four.
5.4 Analysis Populations

The following populations will be used: Intent-to-Treat (ITT) Population: All patients randomized into the study will be included in the ITT population. Patients will be included as randomized. Ta G1-G2 Population: Patients who had 4 or fewer tumors that were ≤ 3.5 cm each at the time of randomization and who had subsequent histological confirmation from the central pathology lab that those tumors resected at the time of randomization were Ta Grade 1 or 2 will be included in the Ta G1-G2 population. Patients will be included as randomized. All Ta Population: Patients who had 4 or fewer tumors that were ≤ 3.5 cm each at the time of randomization and who had subsequent histological confirmation from the central pathology lab that those tumors resected at the time of randomization were Ta will be included in the Ta G1-G2 population. Patients will be included as randomized. Ta G3 Population: Randomized patients with baseline Ta G3 histology by central pathology will be included in this population. Patients will be included as randomized. Tis Population: Randomized patients with baseline Tis tumor stage by central pathology will be included in this population. Patients will be included as randomized. T1 Population: Randomized patients with baseline T1 tumor stage by central pathology will be included in this population. Patients will be included as randomized. T2 Population: Randomized patients with baseline T2 tumor stage by central pathology will be included in this population. Patients will be included as randomized. Per Protocol Population: Patients who had 4 or fewer tumors that were ≤ 3.5 cm each at the time of randomization and who had subsequent histological confirmation from the independent central pathology laboratory that those tumors resected at the time of randomization were Ta G1-G2 will be included in the Ta G1-G2 population. Patients who receive any further intravesical therapy for bladder cancer (beyond randomized treatment) for any reason will not be included in this population. Patients will be included as treated. Since the Per Protocol Population closely reflect Ta G1 G2 Population except for actual treatment assignment if the randomization is violated, the PP analysis will be provided only for primary endpoint. Safety Population: Safety analysis will include all patients randomized to the TURBT plus study drug (EOquin or placebo) and have received an instillation of EOquin or placebo, regardless of duration of retention. Patients who have been randomized to the TURBT plus study drug group, but did not receive TURBT or study drug will be excluded from the safety population.
5.5 Analysis Variables
Some of the key variables are listed below:
5.5.1 Demographic and Baseline Characteristic Variables
Gender
Race
Age
Site of bladder tumors
Number of bladder tumors
Size of bladder tumors
Stage of bladder tumors
Grade of bladder tumors
Primary versus recurrent tumors
Number of prior recurrences
Number of prior intravesical therapies
Medical history
Physical examination
Vital signs
Smoking status
5.5.2 Efficacy Variables
The primary efficacy endpoint is recurrence rate at 2 years Secondary efficacy endpoints, ranked by clinical relevance, are:
Time to recurrence
Time to progression
Progression rate at 2 years
Number of recurrences within 2 years
Disease-Free Survival
Disease-Free Interval
Overall Survival

The analyses of efficacy endpoints will employ a hierarchical closed testing procedure, where endpoints are tested in sequence. The order of the endpoints include 1) Primary endpoint - Recurrence Rate, 2) Secondary Endpoint #1 - Time to Recurrence. No adjustment to alpha will be necessary, with each test at the same significance level of α = 0.05, but no
confirmatory claims can be based on an endpoint with a rank lower than an endpoint whose null hypothesis could not be rejected at the 0.05 level.
5.5.2.1 Algorithm for the derivation of recurrence rate, time to recurrence, progression
and time to progression The study efficacy dataset for the study has the following variables:
1. Time of Instillation relative to TURBT
a. Date/time of TURBT at Week 0 – This should be the randomization time point or
Baseline
b. Date/time of instillation at Week 0
This Date/Time will be used to calculate the time of instillation relative to TURBT – an important variable for all subset analysis of interest: 0-30 min, 31-90min, >90 min, etc.
2. Recurrence rate and time to recurrence – following variables are available.
a. TURBDT – date and time of randomization/TURBDT, the visit is labeled as visit=3
and all subsequent visit designation will be shifted to visit=2 in the dataset as opposed to protocol to be consistent with central pathology report data structure.
b. Date of TUR is collected in the study – This is the time of resection. Not all patients
go through resection when the tumor is found during the scheduled cystoscopy. Even if they get resection, the time of resection may be much later than the time of tumor observed.
c. Date of Cystoscopy – performed every 3 months. If tumor is found, the biopsy is
performed and samples will be sent to central pathology lab.
d. Pathology report date for all visits – when cystoscopy is performed, if tumor is seen
by local cystoscopy, a biopsy is performed and the samples are sent to pathology lab. This is the report date. The report date may be much lagged (especially central
laboratory) due to review and report creation at the central pathology lab. The
following data will be available.
i. Date of local pathology reports
ii. Date of central/Bostwick pathology reports – Data from Central/Bostwick
pathology reports should be used for stage and grade for all efficacy analysis.
e. Pathology collection date – available for all time points when samples collected from
biopsy and sent to central pathology lab. It is the collection date at the central pathology.
f. Tumor found (Y/N) at every visit – this is the local observation of whether tumor is
seen during cystoscopy.
g. Histologic grade and stage at every visit – There is likely two sets of grade and stage,

one local and one central for every visit. Since Bostwick was the local laboratory for some clinical sites, Bostwick was also the local lab. If tumor is confirmed by central pathology, then there should be a grade or stage at those visits from central lab and those grade or stage will be used for the analysis. If the central lab is missing at Week 0 for a patient, that patient should be non-evaluable for the Ta G1G2 analysis population. The algorithm should be the following
1. Recurrence
a. Any re-occurrence of either histologic grade or stage or both at any post baseline visit
should be considered as recurrence. This can include stage (Ta, T1, T2, Cis) or grade (G1, G2, G3, low grade or high grade).
b. The baseline is the Date of TURBDT at Week 0.
c. Use the date of recurrence in the following sequence
i. Date of cystoscopy of a visit when the tumor is histologically confirmed by
central pathology.
ii. If the date of cystoscopy is not available but central histologic stage or grade
is positive, use the date of pathology collection for that patient.
iii. If the date of pathology collection is not available but central histologic stage
or grade is positive, use the TUR date for that patient. The report date is very late and this scenario should be very rare.
d. If a patient does not have a recurrence in 2 years ie when 24 month cystoscopy follow
up is completed (should be the case for ~50% of patients), the patient should be censored with recurrence is ‘No’ and the date of the last measurement should be as follows
i. Date of last cystoscopy performed in that patient by 24 months.
ii. If date of cystoscopy is not available, use the date of pathology collection
date.
iii. If above two are not available, ie, if a patient does not have any follow up
cystoscopy, the patient should be censored at baseline.
e. If a patient died without any recurrence or prior to recurrence, the patient would be
censored using date of death.
f. If a patient died after 24 month follow up without any recurrence, the date of 24
month follow up will be considered as the date with patient being censored.
2. Progression
a. Disease progression should be considered by reviewing only central pathology
histologic grade and/or stage.
b. Sequence of progression for stage is Cis -> Ta -> T1 -> T2.
c. The sequence of progression of grade is G1 -> G2 -> G3 or Low -> High. There
should be no sequence between G* and low and high.
d. Patient is considered progressed if either grade or stage progression is observed or
both. In case of both data available, if anyone is progressed as above, the patient is
considered to be progressed.
e. The date of progression uses the same date algorithm as the Item (1) above for
recurrence.
f. If a patient died without any recurrence or prior to recurrence, the patient would be
considered progressed with date of death as the date.
g. If a patient died after 24 month follow up without any recurrence, the date of 24

month follow up will be considered as the date with patient being censored. The efficacy analysis will be performed only using data from central pathology laboratory. No analysis will be performed using local laboratory data. All local laboratory data will be provided in listings.

blocks.text: 5.6 Pooling of Data

The enrollment is expected to be 4-40 patients per investigative site. Enrollment summary will be provided by site. Summary results of the primary endpoint will be provide by geographic regions (US, Ex-US). Data from all sites will be pooled for the analysis.

Disposition will include following tabulations:
Number of patients randomized into each treatment group,
Number of patients who received study medication,
Patients with violations of inclusion/exclusion criteria,
Status at the end of study, reasons for withdrawal from the study,
Patients in the ITT Population and reasons for exclusion from the ITT Population,
Patients in the Ta G1-G2 Population and reasons for exclusion from the Ta G1-G2
Population
Patients in Per Protocol Population and reasons for exclusion from Per Protocol
Population
Patients in Safety Population and reasons for exclusion from the Safety Population
Patients enrolled by each site.
5.8 Demographic and Baseline Characteristic Analysis

Demographic characteristics (age, race, gender, vital signs, and smoking status), disease characteristics (number of lesions, lesion size and location, and lesion pathology), and medical history will be summarized for the safety population. Continuous variables will be summarized by descriptive statistics (mean, standard error, median, min and max). Categorical variables will be summarized by frequency and percent of patients in corresponding categories. In order to assess comparability of demographic and baseline characteristics between subgroups of patients of various intervals of time to study drug installation from TURBT, the above variables will be summarized for the following subgroups.
a. ≤ 30 minutes
b. 31 - 90 minutes
c. >90 minutes
5.9 Efficacy Analyses
Recurrence Rate at 2 Years

The primary efficacy endpoint and analysis populations are recurrence rate at 2 years and Ta G1-G2 Population, respectively. The number and percentage of patients with recurrence at Months 6, 12, 18, and 24 (2 years) and the corresponding exact 95% confidence intervals will be presented for Ta G1-G2 population by treatment group and Time from TUR to Instillation Group. Treatment effect in recurrence rate at 2 years in each subgroup of Time from TUR to Instillation Group 1 for Ta G1-G2 population will be analyzed using 95% confidence intervals for odds ratio and Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel 2  test. The same analyses will be carried out for ITT, Ta G1 G2 Populations and all population subgroups. Time to Recurrence Distribution of time to recurrence for each treatment group will be estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method and displayed using Kaplan-Meier curves. The median time to recurrence with 95% confidence intervals will be estimated for each treatment group. Treatment effect will be compared by a log-rank test, if the proportional hazards (PH) assumption is basically valid, and the difference occurs late in time between two Kaplan-Meier curves. Otherwise, Wilcoxon test will used in comparison of treatment
effect. A Cox proportional hazards model will be used to estimate the hazard ratio and

its 95% confidence interval. Treatment will be the only covariate in the Cox model. Time to Progression Distribution of time to progression for each treatment group will be estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method and displayed using Kaplan-Meier curves. The median time to progression with 95% confidence intervals will be estimated for each treatment group. Treatment effect will be compared by a log-rank test, if the proportional hazards (PH) assumption is basically valid, and the difference occurs late in time between two Kaplan-Meier curves. Otherwise, Wilcoxon test will used in comparison of treatment
effect. A Cox proportional hazards model will be used to estimate the hazard ratio and

its 95% confidence interval. Treatment will be the only covariate in the Cox model. For this endpoint, the analysis will be performed using ITT, Ta G1-G2 Populations and all population subgroups. Multivariate Analysis of Recurrence A logistic regression model may be used to find prognostic variables for recurrence rate. These analyses will be carried out for the EOquin group. Prospectively determined prognostic factors listed below will be assessed initially as covariates with others added as necessary:
Gender
Race
Age
Smoking status
Site of bladder tumors at baseline
Number of bladder tumors at baseline
Size of bladder tumors at baseline
Stage of bladder tumors at baseline
Grade of bladder tumors at baseline
Primary versus recurrent tumors at baseline
Number of previous recurrences at baseline
Number of previous intravesical therapies at baseline
Time of EOquin retention
The sensitivity analysis of recurrence rate and time to recurrence will be performed for the following subgroups.
Geographic regions: US and Non-US
Age: <65, ≥ 65 years
Gender: Male, Female
Race: White, Other
Diagnosis of Bladder Tumor at Baseline: Primary, Recurrent
5.10 Safety Analyses

Safety will be evaluated from study therapy exposure, reported adverse events, changes in laboratory values, vital signs, physical examination findings, and progression to higher stage or grade. Concomitant medications will be summarized. Summary tables will be presented for safety population.
5.10.1 Extent or Exposure
Time from TURBT to start of instillation, volume of the instillate, and duration of retention of EOquin or placebo will be summarized by treatment group.
5.10.2 Concomitant Medications
All medications will be tabulated by treatment group.
5.10.3 Adverse Events

Treatment emergent adverse events will be collected from all randomized patients through month 6 of the study. After 6 months on study only genitourinary adverse events and serious adverse events will be collected. Treatment emergent adverse events (TEAE) are those adverse events that occur or worsen following the TURBT procedure. Adverse events will be graded according to National Cancer Institute Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (NCI CTCAE) version 3.0, and coded using MedDRA dictionary version 9.0 and grouped by preferred term (PT) and system organ class (SOC). A List of all analyses of AEs are provided in Table 3. Summaries will be generated for treatment-related adverse events, defined as those TEAEs with a reported possible, probable or definite relationship to study treatment. Serious adverse events and adverse events resulting in premature discontinuation of study will be listed by patient.
In addition to overall summary of adverse events, the summary of adverse events will be provided for the following subgroups in both treatment groups.
a. ≤ 30 minutes
b. 31 - 90 minutes
c. >90 minutes
5.10.4 Laboratory Parameters

Laboratory parameters will be summarized over time. For continuous variables, the number of patients, mean, standard error, median and range will be displayed for both actual results and for changes from baseline. For discrete variables, frequency distributions will be displayed. Laboratory values will be graded according to the NCI Common Toxicity Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) in the protocol. Shift tables displaying patient counts and percent classified by baseline grade and maximum grade on treatment will be provided. Abnormal values will be flagged on data listings.
5.10.5 Functional Bladder Capacity

Functional bladder capacity will be studied in a random subset of 150 patients. Three-day voiding diaries will record frequency and volume of urination and will be reported at screening, year 1 and year 2 for both treatment groups. Also, voided volume and post void residual volume, obtained by ultrasound scan of the bladder, will be summed to estimate total bladder capacity. Summary statistics will be reported for all measures of bladder capacity by treatment group.
5.10.6 Other Variables
Vital signs will be summarized by treatment group and time points.
